en: where the bed of us two was,
Before the forest, in a valley,
my beloved had come there before.
so that I am blessed for evermore.
Did he kiss me? A thousand times, surely:
see how red my mouth is.
At that there will still be laughter,
if anyone comes along that same path.
By the roses he may well,
make out where my head lay.
(may God forbid it now!), I would be ashamed.
shall find that out but he and I
that one can surely be trusted.
notes: 'tandaradei' imitates the nightingale's song and is kept as it is; the asterisk is in the source.
2.5: 'hêre frouwe' is disputed: an exclamation ('noble Lady!', perhaps 'Holy Virgin!') or 'as a noble lady' (she was received like a fine lady).
3.4-3.5: 'des wirt noch gelachet inneclîche' is literally 'at that there will still be laughing, inwardly / heartily'.
4.9: 'getriuwe' is faithful, loyal: the bird will keep the secret.
